name: Commodore 64 SID music
lineage: British and Northern European game-music practice of 1983-1992 written for the MOS 6581/8580 SID chip in the Commodore 64, codified by Rob Hubbard, Martin Galway, Ben Daglish, Jeroen Tel and Chris Huelsbeck via hand-written 6502 assembly players — three voices only, so chords are rendered as 50Hz arpeggio cycling, bass and lead share a channel through rapid note interleaving, and colour comes from pulse-width modulation, hard sync, ring modulation and the chip's resonant analog filter, over driving 130-160 BPM patterns whose drums are the noise oscillator with a fast pitch envelope.
